Chapter 1

Getting started

Signing up

Everyone

You create your account once, from the sign-in page, with your own details.

  1. 1Open the site and choose Sign up.
  2. 2Enter your work email and a password.
  3. 3Enter your employee ID — exactly 9 digits, including any leading zeros (for example 001895123) — your name, position, address, phone number and emergency contact.
  4. 4Submit. Your account starts as pending.
NoteAn administrator approves your account and sets your role. Until then, signing in shows a waiting page. Ask your team leader if it takes more than a day.

Signing in and the second step

Everyone

  1. 1Open the site, enter your email and password, and choose Sign in.
  2. 2Team leaders, managers, trainers, SMEs and administrators must add a second step the first time: install an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password), scan the QR code shown, and type the 6-digit code. Agents may do the same from the profile panel.
  3. 3From then on, sign-in asks for the current 6-digit code after your password.
Heads upLost or replaced your phone? You cannot pair a new one yourself. Ask an administrator to reset your second step, then pair again.

The header and your profile panel

The header

Everyone

The navy bar stays at the top of every page.

Brand mark
Takes you back to your dashboard.
Your name and role
Opens your profile panel (below).
Inbox
Your notifications. The orange badge counts the unread ones.
Sign out
Ends your session on this browser.
Tabs
The pages you can open. Which tabs you see depends on your role — see page 5.

Your profile panel

Everyone

  1. 1Click your name at the top right. The panel slides in from the right.
  2. 2Add photo under your name to add a picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP). It shows beside your name in the header. Change photo and Remove appear once you have one.
  3. 3Edit your first, last and middle name, phone number, address and emergency contact.
  4. 4Choose Save changes. “Saved” confirms it. Cancel, the ×, Escape or clicking outside closes the panel without saving.
  5. 5Manage security & MFA opens the page where you pair or change your authenticator app.
NoteEmployee ID, position, team leader and manager are taken from the roster once an administrator links your account. If one is wrong, ask an administrator — you cannot change them here.

Chapter 1

Who sees what

Every account has one role. The role decides which tabs appear and whose data you can read.

AgentDashboard · Action Items · Development Hub · Time Off · Stack Rank · My Tools · My Quality Scores
Team LeaderDashboard · Employees · Action Items · Records · Development Hub · Time Off · Stack Rank · MBO · My Tools · EWS · Ramp · Adherence · Quality Audit · 201 File
ManagerDashboard · Employees · Action Items · Records · Development Hub · Time Off · Stack Rank · MBO · Skills · EWS · Ramp · Quality Audit · 201 File
Trainer and SMEDashboard · Employees · Action Items · Records · Development Hub · Stack Rank · MBO · Quality Audit · 201 File
AdministratorDashboard · Analytics · Action Items · Records · Development Hub · Time Off · Stack Rank · MBO · Skills · EWS · Ramp · Quality Audit · 201 File · Import · Users

What the roles mean

  • ·Agent — sees their own numbers, action items, quality scores and tools.
  • ·Team Leader — works their own roster: coaching, time off, early warning signs, ramp, adherence, audits, and the 201 file of their direct reports.
  • ·Manager — the same over every team in their span, with a per-team-leader roll-up.
  • ·Trainer and SME — the support group. They see every employee and can file quality audits on anyone, but have no roster of their own, so no Time Off, EWS, Ramp or Adherence. Their audits do not count toward a team leader's weekly requirement.
  • ·Administrator — every leader page except Employees and Adherence, plus Analytics, the data import and the Users page.
TipTwo tabs change name by role: a team leader's Skills tab reads “My Tools” (the calculators), and an agent's My Tools tab is their own stats and calculators.

2 · Your dashboard

Chapter 2

Your dashboard

The dashboard is the first page after sign-in. The period picker at the top (a day, a week, a month, a quarter, a year) drives every number on it.

As an agent

Agent

  • ·The summary on the left: how many of your KPIs you met this period, which groups have something below target, and your action items.
  • ·One tile per KPI, grouped as Composite, Output, Quality and Engagement, each with the target and the change from the previous period. A red figure is below target.
  • ·Below the tiles, the weekly trend of whichever KPI you click — six or twelve weeks.

Reading the numbers

Everyone

Below target
At least one KPI failed its threshold for the period.
At risk
Nothing failed, but at least one KPI is inside the warning band.
With data
Agents who had any measured KPI in the period. Someone with no data is neither passing nor failing.
Sustained
An action item whose KPI has stayed on target long enough to close.
TipA number that looks wrong is usually the period: a week that has not been imported yet shows nothing, not zero. Widen the period before reporting it.

Chapter 2

As a team leader

The summary column

Team Leader · Trainer · SME

Trainers and SMEs see this same view over every agent on the floor. Read it top to bottom:

  • ·Agents meeting every KPI, as a share of those with data for the period, then how many are below target and at risk.
  • ·Passing PAR (the R1–R5 productivity rating worked out from cases and hours), Passing MBO and Failing MBO (the month's objectives) — the last one links to the gates an agent is missing.
  • ·Action items: active, sustained, awaiting acknowledgement, monitoring, overdue, with All action items →.
  • ·Focus Tech: the five agents furthest from target this period, worst first. Each shows how many KPIs are below target or at risk and the measure to look at first. Click a name to open the agent.

The tiles and the trend

Team Leader · Trainer · SME

One tile per KPI with the team average, the target and how many met it — a tile turns red when fewer than two thirds met it. Click a tile to chart it in the team trend. Below, the agent table and “Attention required”, this week's failed thresholds.

Chapter 3

Action Items · Records

Action Items

Everyone

An open performance thread: the failed KPI, the root-cause notes, the action plan and the weekly timeline of every evaluation since it opened.

  1. 1Leaders open an item from the dashboard's “Attention required” list or from the agent's page.
  2. 2Write the root cause and the action plan; the agent gets a notification.
  3. 3The agent opens the item and chooses Acknowledge. Items waiting on this are counted on the dashboard.
  4. 4Each week the item is re-evaluated automatically from the import. The counter at the top right counts consecutive passing weeks; it closes as sustained once the KPI has held on target for four.
NoteHandle-time items carry a Time & Motion call study: time one call segment by segment against a baseline to see which part drives the overage (the same stopwatch as a Phone audit, page 15).

Records

Team Leader · Manager · Trainer · SME · Administrator

The read-only, printable archive of everything written against action items: coaching records, root-cause notes, time and motion studies, acknowledgements. Open a record and print it from the browser for a file copy.

Chapter 3

Development Hub · Time Off · Stack Rank

Development Hub

Everyone

Development and coaching items in progress — the plans that are not tied to a failed KPI. Agents see their own; leaders see their team's.

Time Off

Agent · Team Leader · Manager · Administrator

Request leave, decide requests, and see who is out. Trainers and SMEs do not file leave here.

  1. 1Agents: choose the dates and the type, add a note if needed, and submit. Your team leader is notified.
  2. 2Team leaders: open the request and Approve or Decline. The agent is notified either way. Your own leave goes to your manager.
  3. 3Switch between the team view, the cluster view (every team under your manager) and the leaders view to see who is out when.
  4. 4A request can be withdrawn by the person who filed it while it is still pending.
Heads upIf your cluster shows nobody, your account is not linked to the roster yet. An administrator sets the link on the Users page.

Stack Rank

Everyone

Where you stand. Agents see their place among their peers; team leaders and managers see the ranking across their team or span. The rank follows the period picker.

Chapter 3

MBO · Skills and My Tools · EWS

MBO

Team Leader · Manager · Trainer · SME · Administrator

Pass and fail by employee against the MBO gates — the month's objectives — grouped by team. An agent's own MBO is under their My Tools tab.

  1. 1Pick the period.
  2. 2Use the pass / fail filter to list only who is failing.
  3. 3Open a name to see which gate is missed.

Skills and My Tools

Team Leader · Manager · Administrator

The skill reference — targets per skill and the rating curve from R1 (lowest) to R5 (highest) — plus the rating, quality and NPS calculators. A team leader's tab reads My Tools and shows the calculators; managers and administrators also edit the targets.

  1. 1Choose the skill.
  2. 2Enter the month's figures in the calculator to see the rating before the import does.
  3. 3Administrators: Edit targets to change a target for everyone.

EWS — Early Warning Signs

Team Leader · Manager · Administrator

Retention-risk flags a leader records per agent per week: the signs that cannot be read from the numbers. The page lists the team's current risk; the flags themselves are recorded on the agent's page.

  1. 1Open the agent, scroll to Early warning signs, pick the week.
  2. 2Tick the signs you observed and save. The risk level is worked out from the flags.
  3. 3The EWS tab shows who is at risk across the team.
NoteTrainers and SMEs do not see EWS: it is the team leader's own read on their people.

Chapter 3

Ramp · Adherence · 201 File

Ramp

Team Leader · Manager · Administrator

New-hire nesting: a ramp schedule from Week 1 through Week 8 toward the standard target, so a new agent is measured against the week they are in, not the full target.

  1. 1Open Ramp and find the new hire.
  2. 2Set a ramp schedule with the start date. Their targets step up week by week.
  3. 3Clear it once they are on the standard target.

Adherence

Team Leader

The team leader's adherence exceptions for the team, week by week: log an exception with its reason so the adherence figure reflects what actually happened.

  1. 1Pick the week and the agent.
  2. 2Add the exception: date, minutes and reason.
  3. 3Save. The team's adherence updates on the next import.

201 File

Team Leader · Manager · Trainer · SME · Administrator

The personnel details of your direct reports (or everyone, for a support role or administrator): names, position, address, phone and emergency contact, as each person entered them at sign-up and keeps them in their profile panel.

  1. 1Search by name, employee ID, MSID (network login) or email, or filter by team leader, site, standing, or registered / not registered.
  2. 2Twenty rows show at a time; scroll for more. Each row carries the position, email, phone, address and emergency contact.
Heads upThis is personal information. Use it for what the job needs and nothing else. Every change to a record is logged with who made it.

Chapter 3

Quality Audit — a new audit

The weekly requirement

Team Leader · Manager · Trainer · SME · Administrator

The Dashboard tab shows each agent on your roster and how many audits they have this week. The requirement is 2 audits per active agent per week; weeks run Sunday to Saturday.

NoteOnly the team leader's own audits complete the requirement. An audit filed by a trainer or SME is recorded and shows in History with a “support” tag, but does not count toward the two. Managers and administrators read the dashboard, History and the analysis; they do not file audits.

Filing an audit

Team Leader · Trainer · SME

  1. 1Open Quality Audit, then New audit.
  2. 2In Agent, type part of the name, employee ID or team leader and pick the agent from the list. Arrow keys and Enter work too.
  3. 3Choose the form: Phone, MPA QA, Fax QA or AV QA.
  4. 4The audit date is today and cannot be changed. Enter the transaction date — the day of the call, case or fax.
  5. 5Fill the header fields (case number, call reason, caller type…).
  6. 6Walk through every category on the left. In each, every attribute starts as Pass — mark the ones that failed and add remarks. The live score updates as you go.
  7. 7On the Phone form, open Time & Motion (bottom right) and time the call — page 15. All five segments must be complete.
  8. 8Submit audit. The button stays off until an agent is chosen, the transaction date is entered and no category is still “pending”.

Chapter 3

Time & Motion, History, analysis

Time & Motion on a Phone audit

Team Leader · Trainer · SME

A stopwatch over the five segments of a call — Opening & Verification, Identify the Concern, Investigation, Delivery of Findings, Closing — each against a baseline you may adjust before starting. The same tool times a handle-time action item.

  1. 1Open the Time & Motion button at the bottom right of a Phone audit. Enter the call reference and adjust any baseline.
  2. 2Start call when the recording starts. Close the panel if you like — the clock keeps running while you score the categories.
  3. 3Complete segment as each part of the call ends; Hold pauses for a hold on the line. Reset starts over.
  4. 4After the fifth segment, each shows On target, Over target or Well over, and the seconds are saved with the audit.

History

Team Leader · Manager · Trainer · SME · Administrator

Every audit in your scope, newest first: agent, form, audit and transaction dates, evaluator, score and result.

  1. 1Click a row for the findings, remarks, timings and whether the agent has acknowledged it.
  2. 2Download raw data (CSV) for one audit, or the bulk export of every finding from the tab.
Pass
90% and above.
Monitor
From 70% to just under 90%.
Fail
Below 70%, or any compliance failure — a compliance failure zeroes the audit whatever else passed.

Team QA analysis

Team Leader · Manager · Trainer · SME · Administrator

Averages, pass rates, critical errors and the most-failed attributes over the last 14 days, 12 weeks or 12 months, each against the same length of time before it, grouped by team leader or by manager.

My Tools · My Quality Scores · Inbox

My Tools

Agent

Your month to date by KPI, your case tracker and the end-of-day email.

  1. 1Read your KPIs against target at the top; the case tracker below counts what you handled today.
  2. 2At the end of the shift, open End of day email, check the figures, and Send. It goes to your team leader and you are copied.
  3. 3If sending fails, the message says why; fix it and send again. Nothing is sent twice.
Screenshot: My Tools with the end-of-day email

My Quality Scores

Agent

Every audit your team leader completed on you, and how you are trending.

  1. 1The four figures at the top: audits received, average score, pass rate and your latest.
  2. 2The trend chart marks in red any audit where an attribute failed.
  3. 3Areas to focus on lists your most frequent failed attributes.
  4. 4Open an audit for the findings and your team leader's remarks, then choose Acknowledge review. Your team leader sees the date you acknowledged it.
TipAn acknowledgement cannot be undone. Read the full audit form first — every attribute is there, with its Pass or Fail.

Inbox

Everyone

Notifications: a new action item, a time-off decision, an audit to acknowledge. Open one to go to the page it is about. The badge in the header counts what you have not opened.

Chapter 3

Import · Users · Analytics

Import

Administrator

Upload the weekly performance workbook and the masterlist. Everything else on the site is read from what is imported here.

  1. 1Download the template for the file you are importing and keep the column layout.
  2. 2Choose the file and Import. The summary says how many rows were read, added and updated, and lists anything skipped with the reason.
  3. 3Re-importing the same week replaces it; earlier weeks are never changed.
Heads upThe masterlist decides who reports to whom. Import it before the week's performance file when the roster has changed, or the new team will not show under its leader.

Users

Administrator

Accounts, roles and employee links.

  1. 1Pending accounts are listed first. Check the details against the roster, set the role (Administrator, Manager, Team Leader, Agent, Trainer, SME) and the status to Active, then Save.
  2. 2Link an account to its employee ID so the person's numbers, team and time off line up. Managers are linked by their cluster name as it appears in the data.
  3. 3Set the status to Disabled when someone leaves. The account is kept for the audit trail.
  4. 4The authenticator column shows who has paired a second step.
Screenshot: The Users page

Analytics

Administrator

The org-wide executive report: pass rates, attention and trends by site, manager and team leader, for the selected period.

4 · Routines

Chapter 4

Routines

Checklist

A team leader's week

Monday

  • Open the dashboard for the current week; read the summary and Focus Tech.
  • Check Attention required and open an action item for each new failed threshold.
  • Decide any pending Time Off requests.

Through the week

  • File two quality audits per active agent (Quality Audit → Dashboard shows who is still short).
  • Record early warning signs for anyone you are worried about.
  • Log adherence exceptions as they happen.
  • Follow up items awaiting acknowledgement.

End of the week

  • History: every audit filed this week, acknowledged or not.
  • Team QA analysis: what the team keeps failing.
  • 201 file: anyone new who has not signed up yet.

Checklist

An agent's day

Start of shift

  • Open My Tools: yesterday's figures against target.
  • Check the Inbox for anything new.

During the shift

  • Keep the case tracker current.
  • Open and Acknowledge any action item waiting on you; read the plan.

End of shift

  • Send the End of day email.
  • Open My Quality Scores; read and acknowledge any new audit.
  • File Time Off requests as soon as you know the dates.
TipPrint this page on its own: the two checklists are sized to sit side by side on one sheet.

5 · Help

Chapter 5

Help

I can't sign in.

Check the email address first, then use Forgot password on the sign-in page. If the message says your account is pending or disabled, an administrator has to act.

My account says pending.

An administrator has not approved it yet. Ask your team leader to raise it; approval takes a minute on the Users page.

The authenticator code is refused.

Codes change every 30 seconds — enter the current one. If the phone's clock is wrong the codes are wrong; set it to automatic time. Lost the phone? An administrator resets your second step.

My team leader, manager or cluster is wrong.

Those come from the roster import and the link on your account. Tell an administrator; the fix is on the Users page or in the next masterlist import.

I can't submit an audit.

Look at the note beside the button: an agent must be chosen, the transaction date entered, every category opened (none still “pending”), and on the Phone form all five Time & Motion segments completed.

Where did the Security button go?

Into your profile panel: click your name, then Manage security & MFA.

A number looks wrong.

Check the period picker first, then whether that week has been imported. If it still looks wrong, note the page, the period and the agent, and send it to an administrator.

Support

Still stuck? Contact Leou Alven Comendador at leou.comendador@optum.com with the page, the period you had selected and, if it is about a person, their employee ID.
